title: A 1% Fee Doesn't Take 1% of Your Money
alts: This Tiny Fee Eats a Third of Your Money
hook: A 1% fee sounds tiny. Over 40 years it can take almost a third of your money. Here's the maths, with $10,000 growing at 7% vs 6% a year.
sources: Compound growth: $10,000 × 1.07^40 = $149,745; × 1.06^40 = $102,857; × 1.05^40 = $70,400 (2% fee). Illustrative returns, not a forecast.
tags: investment fees, 1% fee, compound interest, index funds, retirement, personal finance, money explained, shorts
pinned: What fee are you paying on your retirement account? Check it today: the difference over 40 years is huge.
